title: ProcDump targets a sensitive authentication process
description: Detects ProcDump or a renamed ProcDump binary requesting a dump of LSASS, KeyIso or SamSs.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use Sysinternals ProcDump to capture memory from a Windows authentication process and extract credentials or secrets.
hypothesis.rationale: Microsoft documents ProcDump memory-dump switches, MITRE records ProcDump use against LSASS, and SigmaHQ maintains a comparable process analytic; approved diagnostics and incident response can use the same utility.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify ProcDump full, mini-plus or mini dump requests targeting LSASS, KeyIso or SamSs while leaving unrelated dumps, missing dump modes and lookalike executables unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Validate the binary identity, target process and dump destination, then determine whether an authorized diagnostic or response workflow explains the activity.
steps: Review the complete command, file path, original filename metadata, account, parent process and target endpoint role.
Locate the resulting dump, inspect its destination and access history, and correlate subsequent archive, transfer or credential-use activity.
Confirm an approved diagnostic or incident-response case; contain the endpoint and protect potentially exposed credentials when unauthorized.
false_positives: Approved crash diagnostics, forensic acquisition and incident-response workflows using ProcDump against an authentication process

validation.expected_outcome: Match ProcDump or renamed ProcDump dump requests against LSASS, KeyIso or SamSs; do not match unrelated targets, missing dump modes or another executable.
